Confidence interval for the between-site variance mapped through the diagnostics

Source: R/interval-mapping.R
map_tau2_interval.Rd

Maps a confidence interval for the between-site variance, such as the Q-profile interval of a metafor fit, through the informativeness, the mean reliability, the concentration count and the dispersion. In metafor's notation the between-site variance is \(\tau^2\).

Usage

map_tau2_interval(
  x = NULL,
  se = NULL,
  se2 = NULL,
  interval = NULL,
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

x

An optional rma.uni fit of the metafor package, from which the sampling variances, the estimate of \(\tau^2\) and its Q-profile confidence interval are computed.

se, se2

Standard errors or sampling variances of the site estimates, when x is not given. Give one of them.

interval

The confidence interval for the between-site variance, two numbers of at least 0, optionally with the point estimate, as in c(estimate = 0.02, lower = 0.005, upper = 0.08). It is needed without x; with x it replaces the computed Q-profile interval.

level

The level of the Q-profile interval computed for x, a number between 0 and 1, when interval is not given.

Value

A data frame with one row for each of "I", "mean", "J_eff" and "H", and the columns functional, estimate (at the point estimate of \(\tau^2\), when it is known), lower and upper. Its attribute interval is the interval for \(\tau^2\) that was mapped, and its attribute method describes where that interval came from.

Details

Confidence-interval mapping is an experimental extension beyond Lee (2026); its interface may change in a later 0.x release.

The informativeness and the mean reliability increase with \(\tau^2\), so the interval between their values at the ends of a confidence interval \(C\) has the coverage of \(C\). So does the interval of the concentration count when the sampling variances differ; when they are all equal the count is \(J\) whatever \(\tau^2\) is, and its interval is the single value \(J\). The dispersion \(H\) first rises and then falls; its interval is the image \([\min_C H, \max_C H]\), which covers the true value at least as often as \(C\) covers \(\tau^2\). These are frequentist intervals, conditional on the sampling variances like the rest of the package; they are not posterior intervals.

For a metafor fit the interval is the Q-profile interval for the model of the fit, moderators included. poolinfo computes it for every estimator, also for GENQ and GENQM fits, whose own confint() uses another method, and the result does not depend on the units of the effects. A fit without a between-site variance (method = "FE", "EE" or "CE") is an error.

See also

metafor-methods for profiles and posteriors of metafor fits, and vignette("meta-analysis") for an example.

Examples

map_tau2_interval(se = eight_schools$se, interval = c(estimate = 20, lower = 0, upper = 500))
#>   functional   estimate    lower      upper
#> 1          I 0.11956387 0.000000 0.77246965
#> 2       mean 0.12840963 0.000000 0.76192310
#> 3      J_eff 7.02118867 6.817468 7.89281710
#> 4          H 0.01160368 0.000000 0.02836966
